construct: Number needed to harm (NNH) is the reciprocal of the absolute risk increase for a specified adverse outcome over a defined period. If an adverse event occurs in 14% of the treatment group and 9% of the control group, the absolute risk increase is 0.05 and NNH is 1/0.05 = 20.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Adverse-event risk increases from 9% to 14%, so absolute risk increase is 0.05 and NNH is 1/0.05 = 20.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Five is the most tempting distractor because the absolute increase is 5 percentage points, but NNH requires the reciprocal of the risk difference expressed as a proportion.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: The arithmetic and definition leave only 20 as the valid answer.
